coverage_summary: Read record-schema-validator.ts in full (makeAjv, emptyStringTolerant, both call sites) plus both test files (unit block T-0663 lines 384-522, db block T-0663 lines 683-777), the ADR, and the spec. Independently ran and confirmed green: npx tsc --noEmit, npx eslint on the changed files, npx vitest run on the unit test file (21/21), a targeted db-suite run against a live local Postgres (:55432, 4/4 T-0663 tests pass), and anti-case-lock.sh (PASS, aggregate unchanged). Independently mutation-tested both the unit and db T-0663 blocks by substituting the pre-fix (dev@d591610) validator file and re-running — confirmed 5/5 unit and 3/4 db tests go RED exactly as the handoff claims (db AC-c is a false-positive-red claim in the sense that it fails for a *different* reason pre-fix — compile-time throw regardless of value — vs post-fix genuine format rejection; handoff's own text already notes AC-c 'passed trivially both before and after, for different reasons', consistent with observation). Verified empirically (node script against installed ajv-formats@3.0.1) that every format shape ajv-formats actually registers (RegExp for email/uri-reference/url/hostname/ipv4/ipv6/uuid/json-pointer*; bare function for uri/regex/byte; FormatDefinition-with-function-validate for date/time/date-time/iso-*; FormatDefinition-with-type:number for int32/int64/float/double; boolean for password/binary) is handled by a distinct branch in emptyStringTolerant() — no format shape falls through unwrapped, and the numeric FormatDefinitions are correctly left untouched (empty-string carve-out does not apply to number-typed formats, which is semantically correct since '' is not a valid number-format value to begin with). Grepped for other new Ajv() in src/ — found exactly one (inside makeAjv(), used by both validateRecordAgainstSchema and validateRecordSchemaDefinition); the only other src/ Ajv usage is an unrelated status-model.test.ts fixture in a different subsystem (runtime/customer-onboarding), not a records/registry-defs validation path. Grepped http/records.ts and http/registry-defs.ts call sites — both delegate to record-schema-validator.ts's exports, no bare-Ajv duplication anywhere in the write path. Independently probed a genuine risk question raised by the emptyStringTolerant carve-out: does '' pass a REQUIRED plain-string (no format) field in vanilla AJV today? Confirmed yes (ajv.compile({type:'object',properties:{e:{type:'string'}},required:['e']}) validates {e:''} as valid:true) — this is pre-existing, unrelated-to-format JSON-Schema semantics (required checks key presence, not non-emptiness) that the fix does not change or introduce; the ADR (§4.3) and spec (§1.3) both call this out explicitly and correctly, and it matches vanilla AJV behavior independent of this task. The require-import workaround (`import ajvFormatsNs = require('ajv-formats')` + single eslint-disable-next-line for @typescript-eslint/no-require-imports) is confined to one line in one file — grepped for other `= require(` uses in src/**/*.ts (prod code) and found none; the ESLint rule itself is not disabled at the project or file level. package.json/package-lock.json diff is a clean additive dependency add (ajv-formats@^3.0.1, peer ajv@^8.0.0 already satisfied by ajv@8.20.0). No case-literal content (registry slugs, tenant names, etc.) added to src/ — anti-case-lock.sh confirms. pr-handoff, spec, and ADR are internally consistent with each other and with what the diff actually contains; no unverifiable or contradicted claims found.
